mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a short-term negative reaction in equity forward pricing due to higher discounting, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-inflation policy periods (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to expectations of tighter labor market conditions and higher wage growth compressing corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not statistically significant during UNRATE > 5.5% regimes (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 106.5 for two consecutive months, it signals a strengthening supply-side momentum that is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns in 30% of such INDPRO expansion events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy HOUST over the prior 30 days indicate supply-side imbalance, predicting a negative S&P 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in >70% of such dual-signal events (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months suggests disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as markets price in lower future inflation risk.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three-month CPI declines (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 140,000 in a month, it reflects strong labor market momentum that is associated with a positive S&P 5-day forward return due to optimism about future earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in >60% of such months (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (industrial activity) above their 50th percentile for the past 10 days signals robust demand recovery, predicting a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies exceed their 50th percentile (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling unemployment (UNRATE < 5%), the negative effect of supply-side constraints on S&P 60-day forward returns is attenuated or reversed due to optimism about job creation, favoring positive returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative in >80% of such low-unemployment months (p < 0.05).
